#3229. CION Investment (CION) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

CION cuts debt to $897 million and sets up a new joint venture for loan sales.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

CION Investment Corporation (CION -6.38%) completed its balance sheet deleveraging strategy during the third quarter by reducing total principal debt to $897 million. Management reported the repayment of public Israeli bonds and the early termination of a senior secured credit facility, which brought the net debt-to-equity ratio to the low end of its targeted range. To support this deleveraging, the company limited investment activity to follow-on commitments and formed a new joint venture, Senior Loan Fund Partners, to which it sold $180 million in first-lien loans. Management stated that these actions, while impacting near-term earnings and resulting in a 17% reduction in the 2027 base distribution, were intended to strengthen the balance sheet for future share repurchases.

Operator: Good morning. And welcome to Cion Investment Corporation's Third Quarter 26 Earnings Conference Call. Earnings press release was distributed earlier this morning before market opened. Copy of the release, along with a supplemental earnings presentation, is available on the company's website at www.cionbdc.com. In the Investor Relations Resources section and should be reviewed in conjunction with the company's Form 10 Q filed with the SEC. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded for replay purposes. Please note that today's conference call may contain forward-looking statements, which are not guaranteed of future performance or results and involve a number of risks and uncertainties.

Actual results may differ materially from those in the forward-looking statements as a result of a number of factors, including those described in the company's filings with the SEC. Joining me on today's call will be Michael A. Reisner, Cion Investment Corporation's Co Chief Executive Officer Gregg A. Bresner, President and Chief Investment Officer. And Keith S. Franz, Chief Financial Officer. With that, I would like to turn the call over to Michael A. Reisner. Please go ahead, Michael.

Michael A. Reisner: Thank you, and good morning, everyone. Last quarter, we told you management had a plan to strengthen Cion's balance sheet. This quarter, we executed on it. Repaid $114.8 million of public Israeli bonds in full at maturity. Which avoided any contractual make whole fees prior to that date. After expiration of the make whole period, we also fully repaid the $200 million outstanding under our JPMorgan secured facility. And completed its early termination. Further, we completed a new non recourse off balance sheet joint venture Senior Loan Fund Partners with a large institutional partner. As a result, we ended the quarter at 1.3 times net debt to equity.

Down from 1.52x last quarter and lower than the approximately 1.35x target we previously provided. The execution of this deleveraging plan impacted our near term earnings during the quarter. We reported net investment income of $0.25 per share, compared to $0.29 last quarter. Partially impacted by 1 time non recurring items. Our net asset value ended the quarter at $13.20 per share, down 2.7% from $13.57 last quarter mostly from unrealized mark to market price decreases on certain investments. And distributions in excess of NII. Gregg will walk you through the specific names with transactions this quarter.

Our near term earnings decline was largely the result of strategic decisions we made rather than an overall decline in the credit quality of the portfolio. To retain cash for deleveraging, we made no new platform investments this quarter. Our only investments were follow ons to our existing portfolio companies. New platform investments often provide enhanced economics through incremental origination and structuring fees In this quarter, there were none. In addition, our earnings were impacted by our debt repayment activity. Most specifically the early repayment and termination of our JPMorgan facility ahead of its scheduled maturity. That alone reduced NII by approximately $0.03 per share, due to the accelerated amortization of the facility's remaining debt issuance costs.

We were also impacted by non recurring costs associated with forming the new joint venture, the reduction of a deferred fee on a legacy tranche of a portfolio company as a result of a new prim-and-tuck tranche that we led for the company. The elimination of accrued income on our term loan investment in Thrill 1, Following the company's post bankruptcy reorganization, in which we received a new investment tranche. Together, all these items reduced NII by roughly $0.15 per share. We announced the completion of our deleveraging in our September 29 press release, but I think it bears repeating.

In a single quarter, we reduced our balance sheet debt from $1.17 billion to $897 million The joint venture was also another validator of certain of our loan marks. Last quarter we sold more than $54 million of our assets at approximately 99% of par. This quarter, a large independent institutional partner comprehensively diligence 20 of our first-lien loans and purchase them through the joint venture at $180 million or 99.8% of par. As Greg will discuss, our total sales and repayments this quarter came in at a blended value above 99.6% of par. Further confirmation of certain of our fair value marks. Firstly, investments dipped to about 72% of the portfolio.

Largely because our portfolio is smaller after deleveraging and after selling certain loans to the JV. Where we hold now an equity interest. We expect that percentage to rise as we seek to continue to monetize equity positions such as Longview Power which alone currently represents more than 6% of our total investment portfolio. The media is still focused on private credit defaults and macroeconomic risk. Fitch's U. S. Private credit default rate recently reached 6.3%. Against that backdrop, we are very pleased with how our portfolio is performing. We placed no new names on nonaccrual status this quarter and 97.8% of our portfolio is risk rated 3 or better. Gregg will take you through some of these details.

We previously announced declared base distributions of $0.10 per share for each of October, November and December which is unchanged at $0.30 for the fourth quarter. For 2027, we expect to set base distributions at $0.25 per share per quarter. And here are the reasons. First, we have reduced our debt on our balance sheet which makes Cion a stronger company but also leaves us with a smaller earning portfolio. Second, until we have completed share repurchases, we will be selective about growing our investment portfolio through new platform deals. Resulting in a reduction in the fees they tend to generate for us.

We would rather pay a distribution we are confident we can cover from core earnings than stretch to keep a level that depends on robust transaction activity. We continue to expect the publicly announced sale of Longview Power to a strategic acquirer to close in the fourth quarter of 26. Or the first quarter of 27. Subject to regulatory approval. We expect significant gains on the sale which we believe will provide us with enhanced liquidity and our first priority will be to seek the resumption of share repurchases. We did not repurchase shares in the third quarter and I want to explain why. First, we were conserving cash to complete our deleveraging strategy.

Second, we were in possession of material non public information about David's bridal and Pearl. Which prevented us from signing a new repurchase plan. Gregg will walk you through the proposed David's Bridal and Pearl transactions So I will focus on why it matters to Scion shareholders. David's Bridal is our largest exposure. If the transactions are completed, our consolidated investment will be divided into 2 separately governed companies a meaningful percentage of that investment will be publicly traded. That would provide our investors with visible market values for the publicly traded portion of those investments and we believe will give us a path to monetize and reduce our exposure over time.

These transactions are currently under a non binding letter of intent There is no assurance that definitive agreement will be signed or that the transactions will close on the terms or timeline publicly disclosed or at all. However, we are cautiously optimistic. Last quarter, we said the market seems worried about 4 things. Our marks, our ability to delever, the dividend and software exposure. Since then, third parties have priced certain of our loans at or near par once again. We have delevered below our target. We have given you our 2027 base distribution expectations in advance, based on our reasonable estimate of core earnings and software is still around 2% of our portfolio.

With the Longview sale expected to close in the coming months, we intend to seek resumption of repurchases of our stock at what we believe is a significant discount to its value. With that, I will now turn the call over to Gregg,

Gregg A. Bresner: Thank you, Michael, and good morning, everyone. As Michael discussed, during the quarter, we focused on completing our deleveraging plan as we seek to position the company to recommence share repurchases. We also exclusively focus our Q3 funded investment activity on supporting our existing portfolio companies, and we received approximately $45 million in full repayments from borrowers during the quarter. We limited our Q3 investment activities to our existing portfolio companies for corporate investments working capital, and other strategic transactions. The weighted average yield for our new direct first lien investments for the quarter based on our investment cost was the equivalent of SOFR +6.1%.

As we discussed in previous quarters, the majority of our PIK income is strategically derived from either highly structured first lien investments, or our PIK income is incremental to our cash coupon. Together, these categories represented approximately 81% of our total PIK investment income in Q3, down from approximately 85% in Q2. Over 99% of our PIK investments are in first lien assets. As a result, we believe this PIK income does not compare to restructured PIK income from a deterioration in borrower credit. Turning now to our Q3 investment and portfolio activity. Our Q3 funded investment activity was solely for our existing portfolio companies as we made no new platform investments during the quarter.

We funded add on investments in existing portfolio companies, including Anthem, ARC, Avison Young, Berlitz, David's Bridal, Innovative, STATinMED, and Trademark Global. During Q3, we completed approximately $78 million in investment commitments across 11 existing portfolio companies of which $72 million was funded. We also funded a total of $11 million of previously unfunded commitments. We had sales and repayments totaling $256 million for the quarter at a blended value of over 99.6% of par which included our new first lien senior loan joint venture with an institutional investor. Where we sold $180 million of such loans at a price over 99.8% of par.

We additionally received full repayment of our first lien positions in Giving Home Health, Lux Credit and RumbleOn. As a result of all these activities, our net funded investments decreased by approximately $173 million during the quarter. In his commentary, Michael mentioned the announced sale transaction of Longview Power to a strategic acquirer.

Longview was 1 of our earliest investments within our opportunistic special situation strategy where we identify and acquire lightly syndicated first lien loan tranches in what we believe are quality companies at significant discounts to par due to technical or balance sheet related issues and then may have an active role in the processes that drive the restructuring or recapitalization of these investments to position the companies for future success. Our investment in Longview began with a discounted first lien term loan purchase in September 2018 followed by a series of strategic add on investments. Additional examples of our special situation strategy included our investments in Yachmat, Carestream Health, ESP Associates, McNeil, Pride, Heritage Power, and Dayton Superior.

We have a number of special situation investments remaining in the portfolio that have yet to be realized, and we are actively working to achieve our monetization success for these investments. As Michael mentioned, our NAV movement during the quarter was driven primarily by unrealized mark to market price decreases on certain of our investments. Marks were still somewhat affected by the macro sentiments regarding the potential crack in private credit most specifically the software concentrations within the private capital sector and the potential impact of AI on those investments.

As a reminder, Cion has not been a significant software investor historically, and has only 2% of its portfolio in the software sector with no ARR based loans as of Q3. Our increase in unrealized values during Q3 was primarily driven by our equity investments. Our largest increases for the quarter were equity positions in Carestream Health, David's Bridal, Juice Plus, and Palmetto Solar. Our largest unrealized decliners for the quarter were our investments in Berlitz, K&N and Avison Young. The decline in the carrying value of our Longview Power equity investment was driven by the company's payment of a cash dividend during the quarter.

As we have mentioned on previous quarterly calls, we expect to see significant quarter to quarter volatility in the value of David's bridal equity due to the larger overall relative size of our investment as well as the highly seasonal nature of the company's operations and working capital profile. As we mentioned last quarter, David's is in the process of separating Pearl, David's AI powered wedding planning, media commerce, and vendor marketplace platform from David's traditional retail brick and mortar operations in order to enhance future prospects for both companies. Post quarter on October 22, David's bridal publicly announced that it executed a letter of intent for a proposed business combination between Pearl and K&N Growth Acquisition Corp.

II, a publicly traded special purpose acquisition corporation. Proposed business combination would establish Pearl as a standalone public company and is expected to accelerate growth and innovation through its proprietary AI technology, scalable pure play online business model, and continue synergistic relationship with David's Bridal established physical retail business. The executed letter of intent values Pearl at a pro forma enterprise value of $350 million and contemplates a $75 million PIPE investment transaction. The parties are working towards the completion of definitive agreements. The targeted closing date for the proposed transaction is during the first half of 27, subject to the completion of definitive agreements and the satisfaction of closing conditions.

Last quarter, we discussed the bankruptcy of Thrill 1, During Q3, Thrill 1 exited bankruptcy with a plan of reorganization whereby our legacy term loan investment was exchanged into a new investment tranche. While this transaction was contemplated and valued in Q2, the exchange resulted in a realized loss on the legacy term loan investment with the unrealized value of the new reorganized investment tranche in Q3. From a portfolio credit perspective, our non accruals amounted to 1.63% and 4.85% of the total investment portfolio at fair value and amortized cost, respectively. At the end of Q3 which increased from 1.44% and 4.41%, respectively, at the end of Q2.

There were no new names added or removed from nonaccrual status in Q3, and the changes in percentages were driven by the decrease in total portfolio value primarily due to the execution of our deleveraging plan. On an absolute basis, non accruals continue to be in line with historical experience and we are pleased with the continued credit performance of our portfolio, particularly in the current macro environment. Overall, our portfolio remains defensive in nature with approximately 72% in first-lien investments. As Michael discussed, we expect the percentage of first lien in the portfolio to increase over the next few quarters as we seek to monetize equity investments such as Longview Power.

Approximately 98% of our portfolio remains risk rated 3 or better. We ended the third quarter with what we believe is a strong and flexible balance sheet with about $1.4 billion in unencumbered assets a strong debt service capacity with an interest coverage ratio of about 1.6x. Turning to distributions. During the third quarter, we paid monthly base distributions to our shareholders totaling $0.30 per share. As a result, the trailing 12 month distribution yield through the third quarter based on the average NAV was about 9.4% and the trailing 12 month distribution yield based on the quarter end market price was 17.9%. As announced this morning, we declared our first quarter 27 monthly base distributions totaling $0.25 per share. Which is $0.05 per share or 17% lower than the fourth quarter. Due to the reduction in the size of our portfolio and our quarterly deleveraging activities. The first quarter base distribution will be paid monthly in January and February at $0.08 per share and March at $0.09 per share. Okay.

With that, I will now turn the call back to the operator will open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. We will now be conducting a question and answer session. Pressing the star key. Thank you. The first question comes from the line of Erik Zwick with Lucid Capital Markets. Please proceed.

Erik Zwick: Thanks. Good morning, everyone. Wanted to start with a question on the DAVIDsBridal transaction. I believe K&N Growth Acquisition Corp. #3228. Is Claude Code truly faster with message threads? I did the math on my logs

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Claude Code’s update could save you time during demanding, hours-long coding sessions at no extra cost. But by how much? Here's my real-world result.

Anthropic yesterday introduced message threads as part of Claude’s Messages API. Don’t confuse message threads with traditional human-to-human discussion threads. With message threads, entire conversations no longer have to be resent with each API call, saving roughly 35% of time-to-first-token when Claude requests contain 500,000 to 1 million tokens.

This feature is on by default for most Claude Code users. API users can turn it on using the “thread” parameter for API requests.

Token consumption remains unchanged, so this capability doesn’t provide a cost savings. The 35% savings is Anthropic’s measurement.

Also: Claude Code’s revised projects adds AI orchestration, but local developers must wait

Timing data from roughly 980 turns in my own Claude Code logs before this feature became available shows that Claude usually began a response about 3 seconds after each mid-task request when running contexts of 500,000 tokens and up. During five busy evenings last month, my conversations made roughly 100 to 225 model calls in a four hour stretch.

Using Anthropic’s reported 35% median time-to-first token reduction in a quick projection, Claude estimated a 2- to 4-minute savings per four hour work session.

Agents often send a bunch of requests to the model during each conversation. Before message threads, each message sent the entire conversation with each request.

Imagine if you’re in a very long texting chat with a friend. Now imagine if every time you sent a text to that friend, you also had to send every other text and every other reply along with that original text. That’s how model messaging has always worked. Except now, with message threads, there’s a better way.

Also: 75% of developers I surveyed prefer Claude Code – here’s why they choose it over Codex

With message threads turned on, agents only have to send what’s changed since the last turn. This reduces the amount of data transmission and increases responsiveness, what Anthropic calls time-to-first-token.

The benefit is seen most strongly in sessions that have a context of 500,000 to a 1 million tokens. About half of my sessions hit that context ceiling multiple times a night.

Anthropic reports that Claude’s message threads reduce median time-to-first-token by 35% for large requests. While my estimated savings of several minutes per session isn’t huge, the benefit increases with very long-running coding agents, and agents that transmit documents and image-heavy workloads.

For computer-using agents, all those screenshots “stay with the thread instead of being re-uploaded on every turn,” according to the Anthropic blog post on the feature.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code

While the time savings may not seem huge, in larger enterprise deployments or deployments where you want the AI to respond faster, any reduction in latency is a big deal and will be seen in any application of Claude technology that has a lot of back-and-forth turns with large data payloads.

Even though the addition of threads to the Messages API can reduce latency, token usage and therefore cost won’t go down. That’s because the model itself will still process the full conversation during every turn. Rate limits also don’t change.

Message threads and prompt caching can work together to reduce workload. Prompt caching has been around for about two years now, and it does save money. That’s because prompt caching allows the model to avoid re-processing prompts over and over (for example, in looping analysis calls).

On the other hand, the message threads capability does offer an extra smidge of performance, at no extra cost. So, there’s that.

Context is the size of the full session that Claude is currently working with. The rough human equivalent is current working or short-term memory. Most Claude Code sessions max out at a million token context, where a locally-hosted AI on my 128GB Mac Studio handles a context no bigger than 64K, or about 6% of the Claude Code context size.

Also: After the vibe-coding rush comes the debugging hangover

Compaction is a process where the AI attempts to reduce and eliminate extra information to fit the current session’s turns into the available context. An oversimplified analog is when you save a JPEG with quality turned way down in order to save space. You lose a lot of the visual fidelity, but you still get the main idea.

The larger the context you have, the longer you can go before the session has to initiate compaction. But there’s a gotcha. The larger the context you have, the more chance there is the model will lose track of what it’s working on or make reasoning errors.

Individual one-off requests also won’t see an improvement from message threads. Also, any conversation that delays longer than 5 minutes between turns will send the full message contents and not just the new stuff.

This feature doesn’t eliminate context management or compaction. But if your context is quite large, it will make responses a bit snappier.

Overall, message threads are a good thing, a solid if small innovation that increases responsiveness. While the feature doesn’t reduce costs, there’s also no additional cost for the additional performance, which is itself a win.

#3227. Cult Phone-Maker Nothing’s Mystery Screenless AI Device Is Coming Next Month

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Nothing CEO Carl Pei believes your work tools can be cool too. He's building one to prove it.

In the introduction to the essay published on X by Nothing CEO Carl Pei on Wednesday, it almost sounds like he’s arguing against the premise of standalone AI devices.

In Pei’s post, he suggests AI’s “iPhone moment” is still several years away. This could read as though Nothing is holding its horses rather than diving into the fray right now. But that isn’t the case; in fact, it’s quite the opposite.

“Our first AI-native product ships next month,” Pei says. “It’s a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product. It has no new screen, and it couldn’t have been an app.”

Pei is playing it characteristically coy. He’s dropping clues, and you can bet there will be more to come in the ensuing days and weeks up until the official launch of this mystery product.

Standalone AI devices are a burgeoning industry, even if they’re yet to result in a hugely compelling, must-have consumer product. Whether it be pins, pendants, glasses, headphones or tabletop devices, tech companies are flooding the market with new native AI devices. Some companies, such as OpenAI, are working on ideas behind closed doors, whereas others, such as AI note-taking experts Plaud, are already establishing a strong and loyal customer base.

British startup Nothing is predominantly known for its retro-inspired audio products and cool smartphones, around which the company is building a cult following as an alternative to more mainstream, generic phone companies. It’s more closely aligned with lifestyle and fashion brands than most of its tech brethren. In spite of this, it sounds like its first AI device will be more work than play.

Just like computers, AI will need to prove itself in the realm of productivity — the workplace — before it spills over into being truly useful and appreciated in our personal lives, writes Pei. And so, Nothing is building a tool for the workplace, albeit one with the company’s customary design-forward approach.

“We were taught that seriousness and beauty could not share a room,” says Pei. But he wants you to know that work tools can be beautiful, and he promises Nothing’s will be.

This is all very mysterious — perhaps more so because the image accompanying Pei’s post actually looks like it could be a snapshot of one of many different smartphones from the past decade or more. The simple black rectangle with one rounded corner looks distinctly unlike a Nothing device, and something a less imaginative tech company might produce.

We shouldn’t be fooled by this, though. Nothing has yet to bore us with a design, and it seems unlikely to start now — especially after Pei’s treatise on the subject. No doubt there will be more hints forthcoming, as Nothing gears up to persuade you that its products belong just as much in your office as at a warehouse rave in Berlin, and that its approach to AI is essential to your workflow above and beyond the offerings of its strait-laced competitors.

#3226. Bread as a Sponge for Oil Is the Best Kitchen Hack I Learned All Year

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Oily pans, stews and sauces are no match for the bread sponge trick.

If you want to degrease a pan or the top layer of an oily sauce without ruining a sponge, a single slice of bread could be your new favorite cleaning sidekick.

While we have vastly improved how we dispose of most things, excess cooking grease still presents a problem. Down the sink? Not advisable. Neither is the dishwasher—even the garbage bin can become a gnarly affair.

Getting the bulk of the grease out of a pan after cooking a batch of bacon or burgers is a good first step, but that greasy pan will either take down a sponge or half a roll of paper towels. What if a humble slice of past-its-prime sandwich bread was the all-natural solution for greasy pans you’ve been looking for?

It’s cheap and easy, and you can toss the used-up bread into a compost bin or countertop food waste processor without disrupting its yuck-free operation.

So, is it ever OK to pour excess grease or used cooking oil down the sink? Even if you run the hot water tap at the same time? Short answer: no. Long answer? Here’s an expert for the “no.” “When grease cools, it solidifies, coating the interior of the pipe,” says Jacylyn Basilone, chief operating officer of Brooks Plumbing. Even if you’re running hot water, the grease will eventually cool further down the line and cause future problems. “Over time, the solidified grease in the pipes can catch debris, thus making a partial clog grow larger and larger,” she says, reducing the pipe’s circumference little by little if you do this repeatedly.

Unlike a clogged shower drain, which you can usually clear easily, “a normal sewer machine or ‘snake’ can’t alleviate this type of stoppage,” says Basilone. “While grease solidifies, it can’t be captured by the claw head. Grease removal is best remediated with a hydrojetter, which tends to be more expensive than the traditional drain-cleaning services.”

Bread is the real answer, and I can’t believe I haven’t been doing this all along. (*Hangs head in shame, fully guilty of relying on the obviously very sketchy hot water method.*)

Bread has always been a superb grease-mopping tool; we usually think of it in a culinary context rather than for waste removal. Just as you’d drag a crusty baguette or hunk of ciabatta across the drippings on your plate, bread is an excellent sponge for all manner of oil, whether or not it is appealing to consume. Using bread to soak up excess oil essentially turns liquid food waste into a solid, making disposal much easier.

If it’s not obvious, this is also a great way to use bread that might otherwise go to waste: the ends of the loaf you can’t bring yourself to eat, or bread that’s gone stale or is starting to show the first mold spores. If you’re going to discard the bread anyway, at least put it to good use.

The bread trick comes in handy in almost endless ways. If there’s a pool of oil, it’s the mop for the job. I initially tried it after cooking bacon. A single, small slice of bread was enough to absorb what was easily four to six ounces of liquid grease left in the pan. I dragged the slice around the pan like a mop, but even after letting it sit a few extra moments, it kept working and eventually soaked up all the liquid grease. (If you’re feeling indulgent and used a fresh bread slice for this purpose, the temptation to make pretty epic croutons here is quite strong — another upside.)

If your air fryer has space between the drawer and the basket, you can place the bread there to soak up grease while cooking. Even for oily, slow-cooked proteins like pork shoulder, you can press the bread onto the meat to soak up grease before serving.

Once the bread has absorbed the oil and needs discarding, responsible food-waste methods are much easier to manage. Depending on how much oil the bread has absorbed, you can safely put the soaked bread in the compost bin or countertop composter without risking a major oil spill and a mess to clean up later. Oil can slow decomposition, so composting large amounts isn’t recommended. Small amounts, such as a few tablespoons at a time, are safe.

Even if you have no other option but to throw it away — and if that is the case, please consider getting a small composting appliance — at the very least, you’re not involving an easily recyclable glass container.

For more home tips, learn this neat trick for reusing frying oil and learn the 10 worst things to pour down your drain.

#3225. This clever banking scam keeps phishing by faking its own demise – how it works

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

You won't see the 'suspended' sign because it's not meant for you.

KELA researchers have exposed an active financial-scam infrastructure that hosts hundreds of fraudulent websites capable of faking their own suspensions to stay online. As of Oct. 25, 2026, 248 financial scam and phishing domains tied to 189 major US banks and financial services have been linked to the same infrastructure.

According to the cybersecurity firm’s report, published on Tuesday, the “Suspended” infrastructure operation runs websites that have cloned the official domains of victim organizations, with a particular focus on business banking. Many domains use the [keyword]-[bank].com format, slotting in keywords such as “secure,” “disable,” “protect,” and “cancel.”

Also: Beware of Bluetooth sniffers: How your favorite gadgets could be exposing your data

A handful of servers spread across two shared hosting providers run the backend of Suspended infrastructure, which has also been tied to phishing campaigns targeting cryptocurrency exchanges and government services in the UK, the Netherlands, Australia, and New Zealand. As a result, the researchers believe that either a single operator is behind the setup or that the server infrastructure is part of a wider phishing-as-a-service platform.

This phishing campaign stands out because of how the cybercriminals behind the scam are protecting it: by issuing takedown notices.

When you visit a website and see a message that it has been taken down or suspended, it’s usually because the domain has been associated with malicious or illegal activity, including phishing and scams. Law enforcement agencies, often with help from technology firms, find these websites, obtain the necessary court orders, and seize the infrastructure or accounts behind them to force a suspension through a registrar or hosting provider.

You see the notice, you move on — and this also goes for scanners and security teams.

However, in this case, the scam artists created a mechanism to show it themselves, to avoid being flagged and taken down. But it’s when they show it that matters.

The false suspension notice appears deceptively simple at first glance. A phishing kit embedded in the domain registers the IP address of each visitor, and on their second visit, they are shown a fake “account suspended” page. The kit is disguised as a challenge page similar to those legitimately used by Cloudflare.

Researchers also detected other decoys, including “Sorry, you’ve been blocked” notices, blank pages, and redirections to Google. Some pages also have reCAPTCHAs, and the researchers detected scripts that block browser developer tools, likely to slow analysis.

Also: Don’t use Muse? Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages – here’s how

But why show fake suspension notices in the first place? To scanners and cybersecurity teams, it looks like someone else has already dealt with the malicious domain, and they can move on to the next suspicious website.

“That design targets exactly the people who could shut a site down,” KELA says. “A victim typically follows a link once. A scanner, a security team or a takedown provider checks a reported site and then checks it again to confirm, and the second check shows what looks like a completed takedown.”

As shown in the image below, while scanners would detect a suspension notice, victims would still see the cloned website, complete with lures to entice them into entering their information, leading to financial fraud and potentially identity theft. After all, one visit is enough.

As of this writing, there are 248 live domains, plus those taken offline after the researchers disclosed their findings to law enforcement; over 300 scam domains have been hosted on the same infrastructure since May this year. Unfortunately, this phishing campaign remains active, with new domains appearing every day.

One lead could reveal the operator: a remote desktop connection to the malicious infrastructure through a standard UK home broadband connection, but it has not been verified.

Use a phishing link checker to verify whether a URL is trustworthy, and remember that any email or message claiming to be from your bank may be fraudulent.

Typical signs of a bank phishing email include:

When it comes to organizations, KELA has released a free Bank Phishing Check tool that compares official domains and organizations against the websites uncovered during the firm’s research.

#3222. Roku is taking away a fan-favorite screensaver – but you have alternatives

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

One of Roku's most popular screensavers is about to make its last splash. Here’s how to switch before Dec. 1.

A fan-favorite Roku screensaver is going away, and users aren’t happy.

Over the last several days, users with the Aquatic Life aquarium screensaver set as the default have noticed a message appearing when the screensaver opens. “Starting Dec. 1, 2026,” the message reads, “the Aquatic Life screensaver will no longer be available, and your screensaver will switch to Roku City.”

Also: The free Roku City screensaver game has me hooked

The screensaver, which displays a digital aquarium with tropical fish swimming back and forth, was available as a downloadable theme pack and was a popular pick for many years.

Users on Reddit quickly lamented the loss in many posts, with dozens noting that the aquarium was part of their daily routine. Roku responded to one post, saying, “That makes sense, and we hear you. Aquatic Life has a lot of loyal fans, and we’re passing your feedback along to the team.” The post noted that when “the fish swim off,” Roku devices with Aquatic Life will switch to Roku City.

You can browse to Settings > Theme > Screensaver to find another theme.

Several online reports indicate that the removal is a licensing issue and that the creator of the screensaver posted on Reddit that he removed the license after Roku’s sale to Fox. That thread has now been deleted, so the comment is unavailable. Roku hasn’t issued any statement of its own about why, but I have reached out to ask. I’ve also reached out directly to the screensaver’s creator.

If you’re looking for the exact screensaver, it’s still available as a 2-minute clip on Roku’s YouTube channel. It takes a few extra steps, but if you want to keep the screensaver running on your TV, you can create a YouTube playlist with just that video, set it to loop, and use the YouTube app on Roku whenever you want to see it.

Even though the announcement of the screensaver’s departure happened less than 24 hours ago, the comments section of that video is packed with users begging Roku to keep Aquatic Life.

Also: I started clearing my Roku cache, and it fixed my biggest TV complaint

Alternatively, you could open one of the many YouTube videos that have aquarium displays and let one of them run for as long as you want.

There are also several dozen aquarium apps for Roku. I checked out several of them, and while they don’t look exactly like the Roku one, they do fill the void. Note that if you opt for one of these, most of them do have ads that play before the aquarium starts.

Lastly, you can download the original app for your phone or computer from SereneScreen.

#3221. Scientists Build Biocomputer That Runs on Bacteria to Solve Hard Problems

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The study relied on the bacterium E. coli and V. natriegens to run the calculations.

Move over, microchips. The next generation of supercomputing might just run on living bacteria. For 20 years, an international team of scientists has been developing a biocomputer that uses bacteria to process information. Scientists from McGill University in Montreal announced their findings on Nov. 3 and published a paper detailing the results earlier this year in Nature.

Researchers from Canada, Europe, the United Kingdom and Australia contributed to this work, which combines biology with computer science and engineering. The researchers say the resulting biocomputer could be used to solve problems that give standard computers a hard time.

“Electronic (sequential) computers are not meant, or designed, to solve decision trees,” Dan Nicolau, a McGill bioengineering professor and senior author for the research paper, told CNET via email.

Nicolau noted that if electronic computers are to solve these types of problems, the computers will need a lot of RAM.

The study relied on the bacterium Escherichia coli and Vibrio natriegens to run the calculations. The researchers used E. coli because it moves through fluid in a predictable, measurable way and V. natriegens because it reproduces very quickly.

By using live bacteria rather than digital processing, the team says the biocomputer can solve big, complex problems at a small fraction of the memory and resources that regular computers require.

The researchers tested the biocomputer with a seemingly simple math problem called the Subset Sum Problem, which famously becomes exponentially harder as the number of inputs increases.

When the Subset Sum Problem inputs grow too large, the problem is known to give traditional computers issues, such as taking centuries, or even millions of years, to solve the problem.

The researchers translated the problem into a graph that branches off into each possible combination of inputs. Next, the team created a tiny physical structure that mirrored the Subset Sum Problem graph.

Inside the structure, they built a network of tunnels to mirror the graph branches. Each fork in the tunnels represents a decision point, and every possible route through the tunnels represents a different solution to the problem.

The researchers unleashed bacteria, which rapidly reproduce, inside the tunnels. The fast-growing bacteria moved through the tunnels, exploring many routes to the solution simultaneously.

Compared to digital processing, the bacteria are slow. But rather than tackling a problem sequentially, as traditional computers do, the bacteria can examine many solutions at once. And if you need more computing power, bacterial reproduction within the tunnels creates additional processing units to help solve the problem.

The team used automated image analysis to follow the bacteria through the correct tunnels. In this way, the researchers were able to tell which paths through the network satisfied the problem’s constraints.

The researchers were also able to adjust temperatures to prevent bacteria overcrowding while traveling through the network.

Enterprising fans have figured out how to run Doom, the groundbreaking 1993 first-person shooter video game, on everything from E. coli to a thermostat. Nicolau says Doom could probably run on the new system, with an important caveat concerning the biocomputer’s size.

“(The biocomputer) must be huge!” Nicolau said. Because bacteria make slow processors, you would need a massive biocomputer to host enough bacteria to run a video game.

But because no RAM is needed, Nicolau said biocomputing could help to solve the global RAM shortage, and even broaden our understanding of what a computer could be.

“A computer is a device which accepts (input) numbers and gets out (output) numbers. Full stop,” he said. “All other uses of the word computer (are) from our point of view, well, poetical.”

#3220. Data Center Backers Suffer Near-Total Midterm Defeats Across the Country

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

More than 40 voting initiatives yielded almost nothing but resistance to data-center projects.

The 2026 midterm election blue wave, which shifted the balance of power in Congress and across state races toward Democrats, can be seen as a repudiation of AI and the controversial data centers that provide its computing power. Data center proponents have heavily backed President Donald Trump and Republican candidates, underscored by xAI CEO Elon Musk investing hundreds of millions of dollars into Texas midterm campaigns to support the industry.

But in many parts of the country, voters didn’t need to make their voices on data centers heard through candidates. They had direct initiatives on the ballot this week that would decide whether data center projects would move ahead in their districts.

In line with a growing backlash against data centers and AI, voters supported about 40 election-day measures that would restrict the construction of new data centers, with only one result — in Harwood, North Dakota — favoring data center expansion.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, CNET’s parent company, in 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

As broken down by the website Data Centers on the Ballot, Ohio had the most number of voting measures: 21, all of which were in favor of restrictions.

Maine, Illinois, Kansas, New Jersey, California, Florida, Nevada, North Dakota and Wisconsin were the other states with data center voting.

Six elections were held earlier in 2026 in California, Michigan, New Hampshire and Wisconsin, with all of them finding voters opposed to allowing data center builds to continue without new restrictions.

Not all the proposed restrictions were the same. In some elections, voters decided whether to impose a megawatt cap on data center energy use, while other measures addressed specific zoning issues or whether data center projects should require voter approval. Some proposed an outright ban on new data centers, and six of those were successful.

Polls by groups including Pew Research have found Americans have soured on data centers due to high electricity bills, water use and environmental concerns, among other reasons. It’s also hard to separate concerns about data centers from concerns about AI affecting jobs. AI has also become a divisive enough issue to affect midterm voting.

The election results were so bad for the industry that Politico declared data centers to be “the midterms’ other big loser” next to Republicans. Not only did voters enact additional restrictions on builds across the country, but data centers were mentioned in Democratic victory speeches.

“I do not work for data centers. I do not work for Wall Street. I work for you, I work for Ohio,” Senator-elect Sherrod Brown said in his victory speech Tuesday night.

USA Today reported that two mayors, one in Oklahoma and one in Ohio, were recalled after public backlash over proposed data centers.

The midterms might have longer-term effects for tech companies and data center firms. It’s likely that with Democratic control of Congress, there’ll be more scrutiny.

“Public policy is going to reflect public opinion, and there’s been a very substantial change in public opinion just over the last year,” Darrell West, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, told Politico.

Political headwinds from the midterms could lead local officials across the country to gain public favor by delaying or canceling data center projects or putting pressure on the companies behind them to offer more attractive deals to communities. The days of huge tax breaks and incentives for data centers could be coming to a close.

“Now, (communities) are pushing data centers to pay taxes, create their own power plants, pay for their use of electricity and water and contribute to local community resources like education funds,” The New York Times reported.

#3219. Windows 11 can run better on PCs with 8GB now, Microsoft says – here’s why

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Windows > Windows 11

The latest updates to Windows 11 offer improvements in speed, performance, and memory management.

The more memory your Windows PC has, the faster it should perform, especially when juggling multiple apps, files, and other data. My laptop has 32GB of RAM, while my desktop has a hefty 64GB, and both are absolutely zippy. Does that mean computers with only 8GB of memory, or even less, are also-rans? Nope, not according to Microsoft.

Also: How much RAM does your PC really need?

In a new blog post published Tuesday, Microsoft touted the gains in speed, performance, and memory management in Windows 11 achieved by the latest updates. These especially impact PCs with just 8GB of RAM, which can now run multiple apps and files faster and more efficiently than before.

To reach this goal, the company said it had three notions in mind.

The first was to make better use of the existing memory on each Windows 11 PC. The second was to protect the tasks that need to feel instant even as more memory gets used. And the third was to ensure that key apps and Windows require less memory. Yes, a computer with 16GB, 32GB, or 64GB of RAM can better handle more intensive activities. But Microsoft wanted to make sure that systems with 8GB could also keep pace.

Based on its own lab tests of PCs with 8GB of RAM, the company claims that Windows is now 20% more responsive and that multitasking is 40% faster than before the latest updates. Here’s how.

As more memory gets allocated, Windows must move inactive apps and files from RAM to the hard drive. When you need to access those apps and files again, you have to wait for Windows to move them from disk storage back to RAM. Normally, PCs with less memory have to do a lot of this disk swapping.

One way Windows eases the pain of this process is through compression. Here, the operating system shrinks less-active data into a smaller format so it can remain in memory. Though Windows has used compression for many years, Microsoft has fine-tuned the technology to determine how much to compress, when to move data from RAM to your drive, and when to fetch it back, especially on PCs with 8GB of memory.

Also: 5 apps I always install on new Windows PCs – most are free

As such, Windows can now keep up to 2GB more of your active data in memory rather than moving it to storage, Microsoft said. An inactive app, file, or browser that you leave open is less likely to have to reload from your hard drive when you return to it.

Opening the Start menu, launching File Explorer, right-clicking a folder or file, and searching for an item are all tasks that need to feel instant; otherwise, Windows itself feels sluggish. To achieve this on PCs with less RAM, Windows tries to prioritize certain actions you need to accomplish while backing off background tasks like search indexing, Microsoft said.

Here’s one example. After you update your computer and reboot, Windows has some housekeeping to do. But any setup work that occurs shouldn’t affect how long it takes to open an app or file.

Also: How to upgrade your ‘incompatible’ Windows 10 PC to Windows 11 – for free

The latest version of Windows 11 speeds up these types of tasks and interactions by up to 20% compared with the January 2026 version, according to Microsoft.

However, multitasking places the greatest strain on a PC with only 8GB of RAM. To analyze this, Microsoft said it conducted two tests on the same PC with 8GB of memory. One test measured the current version of Windows 11, while the other gauged the January 2026 flavor. Here, the testers opened 20 tabs in Microsoft Edge, kicked off a 4K video, and launched large files in Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, one after another. The current version of Windows is up to 40% faster than its predecessor, the company said.

To reduce the need for RAM among Windows and certain key apps, Microsoft said that it has improved how memory is managed and when it’s used.

As one example, memory is allocated to Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook more efficiently, resulting in a 360 MB savings in RAM. This maneuver also extends to third-party apps such as WhatsApp, which has reduced its memory requirements.

Also: 11 Windows apps I replace on every new PC (and the ones I keep)

On PCs with 8GB of memory, the Widgets app loads only when you open it and frees up about 200 MB of RAM when you close it. In Microsoft Edge, inactive tabs now go to sleep after 15 minutes, down from two hours previously, reducing overall memory allocation.

Across Windows, Microsoft 365, and Edge, those improvements reduced the growth in required memory by up to 900 MB, Microsoft said.

How does Microsoft test these scenarios to see whether the latest Windows updates and fixes are helping PCs with less memory?

“We test those fixes across a broader collection of over 20,000 PCs in our labs, including current 8 GB models, using automated workloads based on activities such as browsing, working in Microsoft 365 apps, joining video calls, and downloading files in the background and even using high-speed cameras to measure the time from an action, such as opening Start or launching an app, to the moment the result appears on screen,” the company explained.

Also: Why your RAM options cost 4X more now than last year

The ability to use Windows without much RAM on your PC is critical these days in light of the “RAMageddon” crisis. With AI companies scooping up massive amounts of memory and flash storage chips, remaining supply is limited, and the prices have surged. The more memory you add to a new or existing PC, the more you’re going to pay. That’s always been true, but now more than ever.

Of course, memory is only one part of the picture. Your PC’s processor and other hardware also play an important role. Here, Microsoft found that a 2026 Dell XPS 13 with 8GB of RAM showed 94% faster multi-core CPU performance than a 2021 8 GB model. But the same 2026 8GB PC performed on par with a 2021 16 GB system. This shows that memory does matter for multitasking, but that the processor also impacts performance.

Whether your Windows 11 PC has 8GB of RAM, less, or more, how can you take advantage of the latest enhancements? For that, you’ll want to make sure that you’ve updated to the newest version of Windows. That would be Windows 11 26H2, build 26300.9818 or later, according to Microsoft. But that includes the latest optional preview build released in late October. If you don’t want to install that one, you’ll be fine with build 26300.9711 for now.

Also: The best laptops: Expert tested and reviewed

To check, head to Settings, select System, and then click About. The section for Windows Info shows the current version and build. If you need to update, stay in Settings and go to Windows Update. Assuming your PC qualifies, you should find the latest Windows 11 26H2 build ready to install.

Beyond updating Windows, you also want to keep your apps current. If you use Microsoft 365, open any app in the suite, click the File menu, select Account, click Update Options, then select Update Now.

With most other apps, you have to update them manually or individually. To ease the process, consider a good software updater program. These will automatically scan most of your installed applications to identify which need updating, then download and install the updates for you.

#3218. UnitedHealth shares are doing something unusual ahead of earnings

The only thing more expensive than health insurance is perhaps the costs of insuring shares of health insurers. Case in point: UnitedHealth Group, which reports earnings Tuesday.

Implied volatility is running at twice realized volatility ahead of the October 13 quarterly earnings release. In other words, options prices - the cost of insuring the underlying stock - are expensive, which sets up well for short premium strategies.

In the case of UnitedHealth shares, traders can sell November premium to cut the cost of a longer-dated January call by more than half. UnitedHealth heads into Tuesday's report with much of the damage from its prior missteps already priced in. While rising healthcare costs always remain a headwind, management's 13% to 16% EPS growth target looks achievable. The stock has basically been flat over the last five years.

By the way, according to the company, 90% of United's 52 million customers worldwide are in the U.S. By its own statistics, the company covers about 12% to 13.5% of the U.S. population.

Growing enrollment is critical to EPS growth, but so too is underwriting margin. In the managed care and health insurance business, underwriting margin represents the core operational profitability generated directly from managing healthcare risk. It measures the financial return an insurer achieves strictly from collecting premiums and managing medical care. On the enrollment side, ACA marketplace-driven enrollment appears poised to decline, a headwind for revenue in a segment that had been a growth driver. Fortunately, it's a smaller piece of the enterprise than Medicare and Commercial. Commercial fee-based enrollment grew ~2.9% YoY between 2024 and 2025, while total Medicare enrollment grew 4.5%. The commercial segment growth may not look impressive as a headline number, but given the U.S. workforce grew ~1.4% over the same period, United appears to be gaining market share.

At 17 times forward earnings, and with free cash flow at 5.7% of enterprise value and 6.5% of market cap, the stock isn't priced for any recovery. On the options side, the market is implying 40% volatility for a stock that's been realizing 20%. Granted. The 40% number captures this week's earnings, and it's likely elevated because the stock has had a couple of eye-watering earnings moves in the past 8 reported quarters. In January, the stock fell almost 20% following earnings, and April 2025 saw a similar sharp decline.

As it stands, UNH is about 12-13% below the midpoint of the two-year high and low. The stock has traded lower in five of the last 8 earnings. Current options prices imply a 6.5% earnings move, according to Cboe LiveVol data. That's the second highest implied move in almost two years.

Sell the November 340/420 strangle to help finance the purchase of the January 2027 400 call. Buying the Jan 400 call costs $18.20. Selling the Nov 420 call at $5.80 and the Nov 340 put at $4.80 brings in $10.60, for a net debit of about $7.60, cutting the call's cost by roughly 58%. If UNH finishes November between 340 and 420, both short legs expire worthless and the January call is held for $7.60, with a breakeven of $407.60 at January expiration. A rally through 420 is covered by the long 400 call. The real risk is below: a close under 340 means buying shares there, for an effective basis near $347.60 including the debit.

#3217. ‘You Can See Everything’ … in Space? A24 Sends Elizabeth Holmes Doc to ISS

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Nathan Fielder's documentary about the former Theranos CEO will screen for astronauts in outer space.

The popularity of You Can See Everything has apparently surpassed Earthly measures. Nearly three weeks after the nearly 3-hour documentary about disgraced former Theranos CEO Elizabeth Holmes premiered in theaters domestically, studio A24 is screening it in outer space.

The studio said in an A24 Instagram post that it has granted NASA’s request to screen the film for astronauts aboard the International Space Station.

A representative for A24 didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

I’d say this was surprising news, yet after I saw the impact the movie had on Halloween, it makes perfect sense. You Can See Everything is a phenomenon.

At my daughter’s school, I saw a toddler dressed as Holmes, which certainly was a choice. People all over my social feeds were costumed as the infamous scrambled-egg bowl from the movie (IYKYK). Heck, the friend I saw the movie with took my idea and dressed in all black, wearing old-school headphones and an emo hairstyle, and carried a laptop to channel Nathan Fielder.

You Can See Everything, co-directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, was initially slated for a limited theatrical release in the US. After three weeks, the documentary hit No. 1 at the box office last weekend, beating DC’s Clayface for the top spot.

Now, audiences around the world are clamoring to get a taste of the movie.

They still have to wait, though. UK moviegoers won’t be able to see it until Nov. 20. It’s coming to France on Dec. 30, and while Sony Pictures acquired the rights to release You Can See Everything in countries like Germany, South Korea and Latin America, no dates have been announced yet.

That said, those lucky astronauts in low Earth orbit will soon be side-eyeing yellow mixing bowls, questioning every move made by Holmes’s partner, Billy Evans, and simply wanting more Amanda Seyfried in their lives.

For a movie that is already super disorienting, one has to assume that removing gravity from the equation will make watching You Can See Everything a next-level viewing experience.

#3216. I tried Sonos’ latest app features – these 2 small upgrades fix big annoyances

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Home & Office > Home Entertainment > Speakers

New Sonos software and firmware updates are rolling out. Here's what you can expect.

Sonos’ promise to release its AI-upgraded voice assistant is nearing its “Fall 2026” deadline, and before fans can use the highly anticipated update, the company continues to make small improvements to its app and player features.

Also: Sonos Ace Ultra vs. Sonos Ace: Who should upgrade

This time, Sonos added System Health, a new in-app page to access a more comprehensive view of your system(s), though it’s only available on iOS for now. However, a new blog post states that iOS and Android users can expect volume presets, more interaction with the app miniplayer, and spoken voice prompts for the Ace Ultra headphones.

I poked around in the app and tried some of the latest features. Here’s what to expect.

If your system consists of multiple speakers, a mix of modern and legacy speakers, or multiple systems, you’re bound to experience a hiccup and be unsure which speaker is causing the issue.

It usually takes me some time to Google my issue and scroll through the Sonos Community forum, Reddit, or the official Sonos help documents to find suggestions and troubleshoot it. Sonos’ new System Health feature provides an overview of your systems, showing your network status and name, as well as the number of speakers and rooms in each system.

Also: I used Sonos’s new home theater feature – it’s a competition killer

According to Sonos’ blog post, System Health can detect a Double Network Address issue, which usually occurs when you introduce a new router to your home or plug a mesh system into your ISP-provided router. The result is two home networks, and your Sonos speakers will split their connection between them, flagging “System not found” errors, missing speakers, or connection dropouts.

System Health is in the Settings tab, under the Help Center menu.

Once you tap into your system, you can see all of its speakers, with unconnected speakers bearing a red “Not connected” badge, and wireless speakers showing a black “Powered off” badge when they’re off.

Then, you can see a speaker’s connection information, including status, Wi-Fi signal strength, signal/noise ratio, frequency, IP address, and more. You can also find its volume output, Trueplay setup status, line-in connection, voice control status, serial number, hardware model and version, and which Sonos platform it operates on.

System Health can also show you your account details, Sonos ID, Controller ID, and your current app build version. System Health comes after Sonos updated the System Updates tab, which now displays an overview of your app, system, and headphone update status. This page also links to the Sonos release notes.

Sonos’ blog post states that this feature is new and still open to change, especially if the Sonos community has a particularly overwhelming response to it. The blog post also disclaims that this feature is a first look, not a deep dive.

However, after a brief first use, I see it as a great way to quickly access all the details you need about your systems and speakers, especially if you’re doing some rewiring, moving a speaker to a new room, or general troubleshooting.

System Health is rolling out to iOS users first. I updated my Sonos app in the App Store and was able to access it, but Sonos’ blog post states that this update is a phased rollout.

Updates to the Sonos app and its player are a long time coming. After receiving several new ways to control your speakers’ volume (I think we’re up to three), Sonos is realizing that granular volume control is a high priority for many Sonos users, including me.

The in-app volume dial is cool, and the interactive volume scrubber is a nice touch, but there’s nothing more jarring than wanting to play some tunes on my kitchen counter speaker, only for it to blast at 80% from when my husband was watching football the night before.

Sonos’ latest big update to volume this time around is Presets, a way to start playback in a specific room at a set volume. I haven’t found this feature in my app’s update yet, but I think it’s because my hardware needs an update. Presets will be available on iOS and Android.

Fortunately, I did use another update to the Sonos miniplayer: swipe to skip. What a teeny, tiny but useful feature. It works just like the miniplayer in Apple Music and Spotify; when the app is open, you can swipe left to skip to the next song.

One major caveat: swiping right to replay a track doesn’t work — at least not yet. Swiping both ways seems like a given to me, so it feels odd that you can’t. Still, being able to swipe the miniplayer to the next track is better than always having the main player open to toggle tracks. This feature is also coming to iOS and Android.

Sonos’ miniplayer is getting so much better; you can swipe to the next track and easily control volume from it, even when you have the Ace or Ace Ultra connected (I tried). The in-app volume dial also works with Sonos headphones.

Also: Sonos Play vs. Sonos Move 2: Why I’d go with the $200 cheaper Bluetooth speaker

Speaking of the Ace Ultra, a firmware update is available. A new Vocal Guidance feature can announce the battery percentage when you power on the headphones, when the audio mode changes from ANC to Transparency, and which device your headphones are connected to via Bluetooth.

It feels like this update is the final stretch before Sonos 27voice arrives, as the release notes suggest. It appears Sonos is laying the groundwork for speakers to support the AI-powered voice assistant in Early Access. Once it’s here, I’ll test it as soon as I can.
